findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The nozzle on the horchata refresher was observed soiled. The PIC was made aware. The nozzle was removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The. Quaternary ammonia sanitizer in the sani bucket was observed reading between 100-0 ppm. The PIC was notified and the sani bucket was remade. Ensure that the concentration of the sani bucket is routinely checked.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed. 
1. The caulking on the utility sink was observed loose and in a state of disrepair. 
2. The coving tiles on the wall behind the soda syrups and the wall behind he fryers was observed coming off the wall.

Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the corrective actions for the areas mentioned above are taken.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed  employee not using a barrier to shut the faucet after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to used a barrier to shut off the faucet after washing their hands to avoid recontaminating their hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The gasket of the walk-in freezer door is observed in the state of disrepair which is allowing cold air to leave the freezer and for warm air to enter the freezer that may result in ice accumulation. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that a ticket has already been put in for the relevant repairs. Ensure that the gasket is repair to allow the door to seal properly to void ice accumulation and other potential hazards.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: At the start of the inspection, there was a soiled spatula placed behind the faucet of the hand sink. This spatula was removed from this location and placed into the triple sink to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure the hand sink is only used for hand washing.  
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The walk-in freezer door is observed to have an accumulation of ice on the inside of the door. Ensure this ice is removed to allow the door to close properly and to ensure that the surface remains easily cleanable. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The gasket of the walk-in freezer is observed to be in a state of disrepair which is allowing for cold air to leave the freezer and for warm air to enter the freezer resulting in ice accumulation. Ensure once the ice is removed that the door/gasket is repaired to allow the door to seal properly and to maintain the door to be easily cleanable. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: At the start of the inspection, there were no paper towels available at the hand sink. The kitchen employee retrieved paper towels and restocked the paper towel dispenser. Ensure the hand sink is properly stocked with all necessary materials. 
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There is observed food debris on the floor between the prep tables near the right side of the hood system. PIC stated they will move the table and clean this area. Ensure the physical facilities area cleaned in detail at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11:No sanitizer bucket was present during the start of the inspection. Once inspector informed PIC of issue, a sanitizer bucket was created and measured at a concentration of 200ppm QUAT. Ensure a sanitizer bucket is available during all hours of operation. 
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The fan in the kitchen, not currently turned on, was observed to have an excessive amount of dust and soil residue. Ensure the fan and fan blades are cleaned before the next use.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee sweeping the floor in the kitchen and then immediately attempt to put on gloves for food handling. Employee was stopped, gloves discarded and employee was directed to wash hands, at which time hand washing was very brief (<10 seconds). Employee was educated that proper hand washing is for a full 15-20 seconds and a barrier must be used to turn off faucet so as to not re-contaminate hands. 

2-301.14  (P) Employee did not wash hands after eating/drinking/smoking. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 1) Observed the food prep surfaces in the kitchen to be soiled with food debris. 2) Observed the coffee makers to be soiled black. 3) Observed the plastic collars in the cappuccino machine to be soiled with powder build up. Wash, rinse and sanitize food contact surfaces routinely. After the prep cooler has been cleaned out and repaired, make sure that cutting board and all food prep surfaces are cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Non food contact surface is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1) Observed items in the bottom of the prep cooler to be probed at temperatures between 48-52F (capocollo was 48F, cheese was 50F, spinach dip was 48F). The thermometer inside the unit read 55F. No temperature log was available. Ham on the top part of the prep cooler was probed at 33F and ice was observed in the top portion. Service arrived during the inspection to repair. All foods were voluntarily discarded and recorded on their tracking sheet. 

2) Half and half and creamer in the dispenser were probed at 55F. Thermostat on the unit read 53F (thermostat continued to go up to 67 during the inspection). These items were discarded during the inspection and unit was taken out of service until it can be repaired.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed capocollo and tomato based sauce in the prep cooler, and the dairy products such as iced coffee and half and half in the customer service area to not have proper date marking. Observed spinach dip in the prep cooler that was dated 10/17-10/26--this is 10 days rather than the 7 days allowed (this was also out of temperature).  These items were discarded during the inspection and date marking was discussed. 

Tuna salad and egg salad croissants in the reach in cooler were not marked with the date of preparation. These were reported to have been made today and were date marked as such.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
1) Observed the fan in the walk in cooler to have a block of ice on the bottom of the unit that was dripping onto the covered container of pizza dough below. Do not store foods under items that have the potential to contaminate them. 

2)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Foods in the walk in freezer are in open bags in boxes with several of the foods spilling out of the bags. Foods must be held in packaging that prevents the potential for contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on the counter in the kitchen when not in use. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Iced coffee and dairy products in the customer self service area are observed cut straight across. Dispensing tubes must be cut diagonally.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.13  (C) Bulk milk container dispensing tube not properly cut. The bulk milk dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than 1 inch protruding from the chilled dispenser. Reference 4-502.13.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed the seal on the right door of the prep cooler at the bottom to be separated from the door. Replace seal as this may not be helping temperature control in this unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Replace seal (specific piece of equipment) with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the handles to the hot holding units are soiled with grease and food debris, 2) the fans in the kitchen are soiled with dust, 3) the fans in the walk in freezer are soiled with dust, 4) the drip pans on the beverages dispensers in the customer service area are soiled with buildup, 5) the hand washing sink in the kitchen soiled.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floors are observed soiled with food debris in the kitchen and the walk in freezer. Clean the floors.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).
